title: The dark room

sources: lights/all.json: camera-obscura-dark-room (Ibn al-Haytham, Cairo, early eleventh century; several lamps outside the aperture, images separate on the wall; light in straight lines; his term the dark room; Kepler 1604 camera obscura)
heroes.html: Ibn al-Haytham (al-bayt al-muzlim, the dark house; vision is reception, not emission; many held that the eye sends out rays)
facts: Make a small hole in the wall of a dark room and the scene outside appears on the opposite wall, upside down.

Ibn al-Haytham, in Cairo in the early eleventh century, set several lamps outside the aperture and showed their images stayed separate on the wall: light travels in straight lines and rays do not mix.
His term was the dark room, al-bayt al-muzlim. Kepler put it into Latin in 1604 as camera obscura.
Many had held that the eye sends out rays that touch the world; he showed vision is reception, not emission.

story: We are inside the dark house, looking down the room at one point of light in the far wall. Beyond it, lamps. The NOOR sphere enters through the hole on a ray of light, shows that the rays cross at the hole and land upside down on the wall behind us, then brushes the old idea of rays leaving the eye away, and comes to rest at the eye of the viewer: light comes in.

world.note: Lamps stand outside the back wall (z below -4). A ray runs straight from a lamp through the aperture to the front wall at z=4; its image point is aperture + (aperture - lamp) * (8 / (-4 - lamp.z)). LampA lands near (1.07, 0.85, 4), lampB near (-0.91, 2.29, 4), lampC near (-0.25, 0.65, 4): inverted, a high lamp lands low.

narration.voice: stand-in (piper en-us-ryan-medium) until the owner's voice tool speaks the script
narration.timing: each line starts 0.3 s after its scene starts; a scene grows to line length plus 0.9 s if the spoken line is longer than the written duration

conventions.time: scene k starts at the sum of the retimed durations before it; event.at and sound.at are seconds after the scene start; the compiler writes absolute seconds
conventions.compiled: film.py compile writes films/<slug>.json (the chapter stage.js renders) from this file; never edit the compiled file by hand
conventions.no_dashes: no em dash or en dash anywhere on screen or in narration
conventions.camera: hfov is the HORIZONTAL field of view in degrees; the stage converts it to the vertical field of view of the frame it renders (vertical = 2*atan(tan(hfov/2)/aspect)), so one spec composes both shapes. hold is how many seconds the camera keeps LOOKING at this scene's look point before it turns toward the next scene's; the eye glides toward the next eye over the whole scene regardless. A hold equal to the scene length means the aim never turns during the scene.
conventions.lantern: lantern.pos is where the light is at the scene start; hold is how many seconds it stays there before travelling to the next scene's pos (hold equal to the scene length means it does not move during the scene); a hidden cue is scale 0.0001 and bright 0
conventions.retime: when a scene grows to fit the spoken line, a hold that equalled the written duration grows with it (it means the whole scene); a shorter hold keeps its seconds
